newsitem.title: USA: U.S spot resids steadied by crude, gas and weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S spot resids steadied by crude, gas and weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held relatively steady Monday in quiet trade, helped by forecasts this week for much colder U.S. weather and sharp rallies in NYMEX crude and gas futures, industry sources said.
"With everything up and cold weather on the way, no (seller) is panicking," said one cash trader, noting sharp gains in crude and natgas futures prices Monday.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $20.25 a barrel, with Feb paper quoted up a quarter to the $20.15-40 level on firmer crude, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was talked steady to down slightly at about $21.00 on reports 100,000 barrels for January 15 delivery sold late Friday at $20.75.
NYPA tendered for 100,000 barrels of 0.3 percent high pour for delivery by January 15. Fixed price bids only were due by 1100 EST Tuesday, January 7.
High sulphurs in New York again notionally were unchanged.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent was flat to up slightly at $18.50-75, with ENEL-spec buying interest seen at $19, traders said.
New York city gate gas prices jumped 50 cents Monday to the $4.00/mmBtu area amid expectations for colder weather this week. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.21/mmBtu equivalent.
